target_profile.system_boundary: Captured HashiCorp Raft Go module: Raft owns protocol loops, replication, membership and snapshot orchestration. Applications inject FSM and stores; in-repository transports and in-memory stores are implementations, not externalized unread responsibilities.
protocol_contexts: Server identity, current term, leader epoch, latest/committed configuration and log/snapshot indexes
unknowns: Detailed failure contracts and implementations of injected stores remain to be examined.

activities.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement

activities.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority
activities.realization_summary: Term/vote-based elections, epoch cleanup, voter lease checks and request-specific VerifyLeader acknowledgments.

activities.purpose: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation
activities.realization_summary: Startup restores snapshot/history; lagging followers receive snapshot then suffix.
Latest and committed log-indexed membership, serialized changes and role-dependent eligibility.
Committed logs traverse a serial FSM queue; callback completion responds to originating futures.

activities.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of support

activities.purpose: Client contracts, invocation intervals and observed completion

behaviors.execution_owner: Raft main loop and per-voter request goroutines
behaviors.protocol_context: Current term, latest configuration and last log/snapshot entry
behaviors.trigger: Follower contact timeout enters candidacy; optional pre-vote precedes a term-incrementing election
implementation_guards: Only configured voters are solicited and the local follower must have a vote to campaign.
Vote receiver checks known leader, candidate membership/suffrage, term, persisted previous vote and log freshness.
Candidate receives replies on a new channel for each campaign; newer terms cause fallback.
writes: Persistent current term and vote; volatile role and leader identity
async_boundaries: Each remote vote has one goroutine and the campaign-specific buffered response channel; old campaigns are no longer consumed.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Election selects the owner that creates a fresh term-specific commitment tracker.
cross_activity_effects.A6: Vote and term persistence constrain later elections.

unknowns: Failure between the two independent stable-store writes in persistVote has not been characterized.

behaviors.trigger: Election victory enters runLeader; stepdown exits it
writes: Fresh commitment, inflight list, replication and verification maps per leader epoch
external_effects: Start peer replication and dispatch a current-term noop.
On exit stop workers and fail still-inflight application and verification futures with ErrLeadershipLost.
async_boundaries: Old workers hold their original commitment and stepDown channels; new leader setup allocates different objects.

cross_activity_effects.A1: New epoch resets support and gates commitment at its first new log index.
cross_activity_effects.A7: Leadership loss does not imply an inflight write was never committed.

Committed entries already handed to the FSM have a separate completion path.

behaviors.protocol_context: Current leader term and ordered local log
behaviors.trigger: Admitted Apply, configuration entry or initial noop
writes: Assign term/index; append inflight records; after StoreLogs success record local match and last log
durable_effects: StoreLogs persists appended entries through injected LogStore
external_effects: Notify each replication worker after successful persistence
important_branches: StoreLogs error responds to these futures and changes role to Follower; local match is not advanced.

behaviors.execution_owner: Per-follower replication worker and pipeline decoder
behaviors.protocol_context: Worker captures one leader term and its commitment object; peer identity is server ID
behaviors.trigger: Dispatch notification, commit timeout, retries and pipeline responses
implementation_guards: Successful append reply records the last entry in that request, not arbitrary current last index.
Higher reply term triggers the captured stepDown channel.
Rejected append backs nextIndex down; missing logs invokes snapshot transfer.
external_effects: Success also drains pending verification notifications as true; stale-term handling drains them as false.
async_boundaries: CommitTimeout sends append traffic even without new commands; heartbeat loop is separate.

cross_activity_effects.A2: Reply term can trigger leadership loss and successful requests can acknowledge pending authority verification.
cross_activity_effects.A3: Snapshot fallback restores followers too far behind for log replay.

behaviors.protocol_context: One leader epoch and latest voter set
behaviors.trigger: Local/remote match increase or configuration replacement recalculates quorum

Quorum match must exceed old commitment and reach this epoch startIndex.
writes: Monotone commitment.commitIndex; main loop copies it into raft commitIndex
external_effects: Notify commitCh; leader processes committed inflight prefix and updates committed configuration.

cross_activity_effects.A5: Committed prefix is handed to processLogs for ordered application.

facts.meaning: For a voter ID in a particular commitment tracker, matchIndexes records the greatest reported matching stored prefix index.
facts.validity_context: Only IDs currently present in tracker voter map count; configuration replacement retains values by ID and a new leader creates a new tracker.
facts.durability: Volatile aggregation over log storage acknowledgments.
facts.recovery: Rebuilt from zero in each leader epoch; local persistence and new replies establish matches.

facts.meaning: The leader commitment object has found a voter quorum whose matching prefix reaches an index at or beyond this epoch first entry.
facts.validity_context: The tracker uses its current voter map and only increases commitIndex after the current-term startIndex threshold.
facts.durability: Commit index is volatile; log and snapshot history are durable through injected stores.
facts.recovery: A new leader re-establishes commitment through a current-term entry; follower learns commit position from append traffic.

facts.meaning: A verifyFuture contains a self vote plus true notifications from registered replication workers, and notifies the leader when its tally reaches its captured threshold or any worker reports false.
facts.validity_context: Registration occurs during one leader epoch; threshold uses latest voter count but registrations cover the replication-worker set.
facts.recovery: No recovery of a verify operation; leader exit fails pending registered futures.

facts.meaning: The stable store contains the last vote term key and candidate-address bytes key written by persistVote; a completed successful persistVote writes both.
facts.validity_context: requestVote reads both keys and recognizes a repeated vote if the requested term equals the stored vote term and candidate bytes are non-nil. The two writes are independent; atomic cross-key crash behavior is not established.
facts.durability: Stored through the injected StableStore; individual write failures are returned.
facts.recovery: Subsequent requestVote calls read these keys, including after initialization from durable state.
unknowns: Failure/crash between the two key writes remains an unresolved fault-contract and history question.

surfaces.reason: Does a same-term delayed snapshot restore an older application state after a more advanced prefix has completed? Sender ordering and legal history remain to be established.
NewRaft requires concurrent heartbeat safety while handler comments require main-thread execution. Determine protection for overlapping term persistence and role transitions.
Determine crash/error behavior between separate term and candidate stable-store writes and whether an old candidate can be reinterpreted in a new term.

formation.explanation: Leader admits commands, assigns current term/index and persists before local match. Peer workers replicate ordered prefixes, backtrack conflicts, fall back to snapshots and report successful stored prefixes. A voter-only tracker selects the majority prefix, gated by the first current-term entry. The leader copies commitment, advances membership and sends committed logs to the FSM queue; followers learn commit position from periodic append traffic. FSM callbacks complete command futures; queueing is not completion.

context.explanation: Follower contact timeout allows configured voters to campaign. Optional pre-vote precedes durable term increment and one request per voter. Receivers constrain votes using known leader, membership, term, durable vote and log freshness. A campaign-specific response channel prevents replies from prior campaigns being tallied in a new one. Majority victory creates fresh leader state and an initial noop. Higher-term RPC/reply, lease loss and committed local removal can end leadership. Pending leader operations fail on exit while previously committed FSM work retains its separate completion path. Startup reconstructs term, snapshot and later configuration history.

connection.explanation: Election log freshness and stored votes constrain who acquires authority over prior history. Each leader creates a new commitment object; late replication workers retain their old object and cannot directly populate the new tracker. New-term noop commitment establishes the prefix before configuration changes are admitted. Membership reinterprets eligible match support by voter ID, while all members retain replication workers. Log matching/truncation and snapshot reconstruction handle old work; committed commands continue through a distinct FSM queue. Verification is another authority consumer: its voter-sized threshold is currently fed by the broader replication-worker set, which is the first focused question.

open_details: Verification eligibility and legal failure history are the selected discriminator.
Same-term snapshot age, concurrent heartbeat authority updates and partial vote persistence remain sourced surfaces.
Leadership-transfer edge cases, protocol-version compatibility and store error semantics are not exhaustively traced.
core_overview.rationale: Representative formation and context paths, their voter/log/epoch connection and supporting recovery/application mechanisms have been read. This is a usable partial understanding, not a coverage claim.
